note: 5,172 support agents, 15 percent productivity gain concentrated in less experienced workers, the most cited field study of AI at work.
title: Generative AI at Work
explain_beginner: Researchers studied how an AI chatbot assistant affected customer service workers. They found the tool made workers about 15 percent more productive at solving customer problems. Newer, less experienced workers benefited the most, while experienced workers saw minimal gains. The AI appeared to share knowledge that skilled workers had learned through experience, helping newer employees improve faster. The tool also made customers happier and reduced employee turnover.
explain_business: Deploying conversational AI in customer support operations yields meaningful productivity improvements, particularly for newer workforce segments. The technology effectively transfers experienced worker knowledge to junior staff, accelerating development and reducing training costs. Beyond efficiency gains, the solution enhances customer satisfaction and employee retention while decreasing management overhead. This suggests AI implementation in support functions can simultaneously improve operational metrics and workforce development outcomes.
explain_practitioner: A field study tracked 5,179 support agents receiving staggered access to a generative AI conversational system. The intervention increased average productivity by 14 percent measured in resolved issues per hour. Benefits concentrated among novice and lower-skill cohorts while experienced workers showed negligible gains. Analysis suggests the AI captured tacit knowledge from high-performing agents and accelerated skill development in junior staff. Secondary outcomes included improved customer satisfaction metrics, decreased managerial escalations, and enhanced employee retention rates.
